gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a 24V inverter's DC capacitors can draw a spike at hook-up that the battery's BMS reads as a short circuit, so the battery shuts off before the inverter ever starts. Epoch's own guide gives the spike for a Victron MultiPlus-II 24/3000 as 'several hundred to over 1,000 A' and the fix as a 47 Ω pre-charge resistor (50 W minimum, 100 W recommended) held for 5 to 10 seconds.
standout_why: Pages checked: the one cited rival (solarpoweredproject.com) plus four other result pages (gesike.com US 24V, ryzzun.com LiTime 24V review, charge-test.com, batterytrail.com). None mentions capacitor inrush, pre-charge, or a BMS tripping when an inverter is connected. gesike only says the 400 A one-second pulse 'covers startup inrush' from motors and compressors. solarpoweredproject says peak current covers 'inverter start'. ryzzun and gesike already cover the other inverter mechanism, the 100 A BMS × 25.6 V ≈ 2,560 W continuous cap: ryzzun works out about 93 A for a 2,000 W inverter at 24 V. ChatGPT's second answer also covers it. So that point is not new, but the hook-up spike is.
decides: This doesn't change which battery to buy. It decides whether a 24V battery plus a 3,000 W-class inverter powers on at all, so any 24V pick paired with a big inverter needs a pre-charge step. It also supports Epoch's specs on paper: 120 A continuous and 200 A for 60 s against 100 A on the Redodo. But Epoch's 24V 100Ah is out of stock at $1,199, so it can't be the premium pick today, and its page lists Bluetooth only, with no CAN/Victron communication. I couldn't confirm a built-in pre-charge on the LiTime or Redodo 24V 100Ah, so a pick card shouldn't claim those batteries avoid the trip.

findings.label: Why the battery shuts off when an inverter is connected
findings.value: Inverter DC-bus capacitor inrush. In Epoch's words: 'Large inverter DC bus capacitors can look like a short circuit at the exact moment of connection'; 'The BMS cannot always distinguish between a real short circuit and a capacitor charging event.'
findings.source_title: Why Your Lithium Battery May Shut Down With Certain Inverters, And How To Fix It (Epoch Batteries, published Jun 22, 2026)
findings.note: Battery maker's own technical guide. The fix it gives is a momentary (not latching) pre-charge button and resistor across the main positive disconnect: hold the button, close the main disconnect, then release.

findings.label: Inrush and pre-charge spec for a 24V battery on a Victron MultiPlus-II 24/3000
findings.value: Spike of 'several hundred to over 1,000 A'. Pre-charge: 47 Ω resistor, 50 W minimum, 100 W recommended, 5 to 10 s hold.
findings.source_title: Why Your Lithium Battery May Shut Down With Certain Inverters, And How To Fix It (Epoch Batteries)
findings.note: Epoch's example uses its 24V 230Ah (C24230A) battery and calls the values 'application-specific examples, not universal prescriptions'. My arithmetic: 25.6 V ÷ 47 Ω ≈ 0.54 A through the resistor at the start, against 100 to 120 A continuous BMS limits on the candidates.

findings.label: Price and stock
findings.note: Maker's US store, which reads 'Sold out. Get an email when it's back in stock.' The Epoch marine collection page also lists it as Out of Stock at $1,199.

findings.label: BMS discharge current
findings.value: 120 A continuous; 200 A peak for 60 s
findings.note: Maker's spec: 'Max Continuous Discharge Amps: 120A'. 120 A × 25.6 V ≈ 3,072 W nominal, against 2,560 W for a 100 A BMS.

findings.value: Self-heating, charge range -20 °C (-4 °F) to 55 °C with heating (cells charge 0 to 55 °C after warming); up to 2 in series / 4 in parallel; Bluetooth app only, no CAN or Victron on the page; IP67; 11-year limited warranty (years 1–3 replacement, years 4–11 40% off MSRP)

findings.label: What Victron integration needs
findings.value: Victron says lithium batteries need communication 'between the power electronics and the battery management hardware', and 'These are mostly connected via “BMS-Can” (CANBus) on a GX device.' LiTime, Epoch and Redodo are not on Victron's battery compatibility list.
findings.note: This affects ChatGPT's 'Victron-compatible' LiTime ComFlex card: closed-loop control needs a Victron GX device, and Victron itself doesn't list the brand.

findings.label: Continuous output limit and inverter headroom (reviewer)
findings.value: Ryzzun: 100 A BMS caps output at about 2,560 W; 'A 24V inverter of up to about 2,000W continuous leaves some headroom'; a 2,000 W inverter pulls about 93 A (2,000 ÷ 24 ÷ 0.9); allows 4P2S
findings.source_title: LiTime 24V 100Ah Battery Review: Specs and 24V Setup (Ryzzun)
findings.note: Named reviewer. This page is one of ChatGPT's results, so this point is already covered there. Included only as context.

unsourced: LiTime 24V 100Ah Bluetooth price, peak current and low-temperature cutoff/recovery temperatures: litime.com returned HTTP 429 on the www and bare-domain product pages and through storecheck.py, and amzcheck.py search returned nothing (Amazon walled it).

Whether the LiTime or Redodo 24V 100Ah BMS has a built-in pre-charge or inrush-tolerant short-circuit delay: maker pages were rate-limited and no manual text turned up. Redodo claims pre-charge only on its 12V trolling battery.
Redodo 24V 100Ah peak current and whether the base model has a low-temperature charge cutoff: the storecheck summary mentions neither, and the product page returned HTTP 429.
What LiTime 24V 100Ah Smart ComFlex needs to talk to Victron (GX device, CAN profile): litime.com was rate-limited, and Victron's compatibility list has no LiTime entry.
